newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian cyclone stationary but still a threat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian cyclone stationary but still a threat.

text.p: Australian weather forecasters were keeping a close watch on a massive cyclone on Wednesday as gales and high winds continued to batter a large area of the Queensland state coast.

Cyclone Justin, the biggest to appear along Australia's east coast for 20 years, remained stationary but still had the potential to re-form and move west onto storm-ravaged coastal areas, Australian Bureau of Meteorology officals told Reuters.
Two bulk coal ports at Gladstone and Mackay remained closed while there was still potential for major crop damage in North Queensland's important sugar growing area.
The cyclone, a weak category two on a scale of five, had winds at its epicentre of up to 120 kph and remained 650 km east of Cairns and 600 km east-north-east of Bowen.
"It is still strong at its centre and big winds and gales will persist for the next few days," forecaster Geoff Crane said.
"The cyclone has the potential to re-form and possibly move west onto the coast, but not for the next 24 to 48 hours," he said. "We are currently considering whether to declare it a category one."

Cyclone warnings were lifted on Tuesday but a cyclone watch remained current from Cardwell in the north to Yeppoon near Rockhampton. Officials would assess foreshore damage as well as possible damage to the ecologically-important Great Barrier Reef, a world-famous tourist attraction, a tourist authority spokesman said.
Most tourist boats and ferry services have been severely curtailed in the Whitsunday islands but normal commercial flights were still operating, the spokesman said.
An Australian military spokesman said Tandem Thrust '97, the largest U.S.-Australian wargames since World War Two was proceeding after being forced to cancel some exercises yesterday.
"We are proceeding towards our objectives but keeping a wary eye open on the weather," the spokesman said.
The land, sea and air exercises which began on Monday are due to end on March 22 and include 27,000 personnel and 200 warships.
Ships that put to sea when the cyclone threatened to invade coastal areas, are returning while fighter aircraft that were moved to inland air bases, will consider returning today, the spokesman said.
